sources.role: existing ADS alerts and phase windows
versioned raw logs and provider-generated line labels

parser_fix.problem: A timestamp-like value in an attacker-controlled request/body could be mistaken for event time by an unanchored pattern.
parser_fix.fix: Audit and Apache timestamp parsers accept actual log headers; JSON uses top-level timestamp fields with explicit offsets. Syslog without year/zone remains unresolved.

transfer.method: bounded HTTPS ranges directly on Thor; compressed archives never stored or fully downloaded

limitations: Historical training environments only; no new independent holdout or incident count claim.
Absence of alerts or provider labels is not a benign verdict. Detection mechanisms, inputs and configurations differ.
Two reverse-shell intervals have contemporaneous raw/AMiner observations but no provider-labelled raw rows; successful reverse connection is not established.
SERVICE_START/STOP res=success proves that logged event only, not full attack success, exfiltration or a production outage.
AMiner includes two TrainingMode=true objects in wardbeck/service_stop; source observation counts are not operational detection rates.
Unknown source year/timezone is not inferred; in-interval counts cover explicitly timestamped records only.
Provider labels are rule-derived, not independent expert incident adjudication. No live MCP trajectory or approved action gold was created.
Partial HTTPS range plus selected CRC/SHA and metadata checks do not prove the full archive published MD5.
